summary: F4 ergonomic review of PR #18 (flatten /specs/cross-cutting/ -> /specs/, 222 files). DX is actively broken post-merge: the canonical entry point an agent is told to read first (per CLAUDE.md) still resolves to the old subdirectory layout, the root-hub-pointers.json registry still emits old paths despite the PR claiming flattening, no CHANGELOG entry tells contributors the topology moved, and the milestone tree carries two M02 and two M03 directories that disorient anyone walking the plan hierarchy. CC-3 confirmed by both F3 (748 stale refs, first-breaker = fitness-lifecycle lanes ENOENT) and direct repo inspection (specs/cross-cutting/ still present with 25+ live files).

findings.issue: CLAUDE.md instructs every agent: 'Read /specs/cross-cutting/root-hub-pointers.json first'. After PR #18 supposedly flattened the topology, both (a) the file still lives at /specs/cross-cutting/root-hub-pointers.json (NOT at /specs/root-hub-pointers.json as the diff rewrites everywhere else imply), AND (b) every entry_points.*.current_path inside it still cites /specs/cross-cutting/<name>.json (lines 34, 41, 48, 55, 63, 77, 83, 125, 132, 139, 146, 153, 160, 167, 174, 188, 195, 209, 216, 227). An agent who follows CLAUDE.md will resolve old paths, then chase them, then either (a) succeed because the old files still exist (i.e. the flatten was cosmetic in handoffs/plans but not in the spec tree itself) or (b) trip a partial-move ENOENT cascade like fitness-lifecycle lanes. Either way the DX contract is broken: the document of record disagrees with the rewrite the PR performed across 222 other files.
findings.remediation: Pick one of: (1) Actually move /specs/cross-cutting/*.json to /specs/ as a single mv + cross-ref rewrite + re-run all gates, then update root-hub-pointers.json current_path values to match; or (2) revert the 200+ cross-reference rewrites since the canonical files never moved. Half-state must not persist. Block any downstream PR depending on flattened paths until reconciled.

findings.issue: A 222-file topology shift with zero contributor-facing CHANGELOG entry. grep of docs/CHANGELOG.md for 'flatten|topology|specs/' returns only the pre-existing architectural-flattening (crates) entries from earlier ADR-0015 work — nothing about specs/cross-cutting -> specs/. Contributors will continue authoring new specs under /specs/cross-cutting/ because (a) the directory still exists, (b) every example in living docs cites the old path, and (c) no changelog signal told them otherwise. This is the textbook 'silent topology change' anti-pattern that the [No silent regression] doctrine flags.
findings.remediation: Add a CHANGELOG entry under the current release that names the move, links ADR-0119 (or its renumbered successor), states the deadline by which /specs/cross-cutting/ becomes ENOENT, and shows the one-line rewrite contributors should apply to in-flight branches. Until the entry lands, treat the flatten as not-shipped from a DX standpoint.

findings.file: docs/decisions/ADR-0119-specs-flat-root-topology.md (claimed ADDED in PR #18) vs. post-merge git log (ADR-0119 = Cloudflare Access gate)
findings.issue: PR #18 meta lists ADR-0119-specs-flat-root-topology.md as ADDED (+116 lines). Post-merge `git log --all -- docs/decisions/ADR-0119*` shows ADR-0119 is now 'add Cloudflare Access gate' per the renumber commit adf9a7c0 ('renumber my ADRs (118/119 -> 119/120)'). The ADR justifying the topology change has been renumbered out from under its own PR description, leaving the PR's stated rationale unfindable by ADR number. Anyone debugging the flatten in 3 months who greps for ADR-0119 gets the Cloudflare ADR, not the flatten ADR.
findings.remediation: Resolve the ADR pointer collision: either (a) re-publish the flatten ADR under a free number (e.g. ADR-0121) and add a redirect note to ADR-0119; or (b) merge the flatten rationale into whatever ADR now owns specs topology. Update root-hub-pointers.json + every file that cited ADR-0119 in PR #18 (~10 callsites) to the new number.

findings.issue: Two M02-* directories and two M03-* directories sit side-by-side. PR #18 modifies INDEX.md in both M02-substrate and both M03-* dirs but does nothing to disambiguate them. An agent (or human) walking the milestone tree must guess which M02 is the active one. The PR's spec-flattening lens missed the parallel disorientation in the milestone tree.
findings.remediation: Out of scope for the flatten PR per se, but DX-equivalent. File a FixupTask: rename to fully-qualified milestone ids (e.g. M02a-substrate / M02b-foundry-preview, or pick the canonical one and migrate the other) and add a single milestones/INDEX.md listing the live set. Until then, every M02/M03 ralplan citation is ambiguous.

findings.file: PR #18 description (verification section vs. consumer-facing migration notes)
findings.issue: Verification covers compile + nextest (2725 passed) but says nothing to a contributor with an in-flight branch about how to rebase past the topology shift. No 'sed -i s,specs/cross-cutting/,specs/,g' one-liner, no list of grep patterns to find stale refs, no callout that 748 stale refs (per F3) escaped the sweep. Contributor DX defaults to 'discover the breakage at merge-conflict time'.
findings.remediation: Standardize a 'Contributor migration' section in any PR that moves >50 files. For #18, add the canonical rewrite invocation, the grep that would have caught the 748 stale refs, and the explicit list of paths that intentionally stayed (e.g. fitness-lifecycle lanes that resolve to ENOENT — call them out as known-broken with a tracking issue, do not leave silently).

findings.file: PR #18 title 'Flatten specs cross-cutting topology (signed replacement)'
findings.issue: Title encodes git-hygiene metadata ('(signed replacement)') instead of user-visible intent. Anyone scanning merged-PR history for 'where did the topology move?' must read titles twice to find this; the '(signed replacement)' parenthetical is noise to every reader except whoever was tracking unsigned-commit f2c0696.
findings.remediation: Going forward, keep PR titles focused on the change; put 'replaces #14; signed' in the PR body. Title-character budget should explain the change, not its provenance.

naming_justification: evidence/debate/pr-18-F4-r1.json conforms to the established multispectrum evidence path contract pr-<N>-<facet>-r<round>.json (12-layer enum: evidence is the artifact-kind shard; debate is the lane; pr-18 is the change_id; F4 is the facet_id; r1 is the round). Matches the same convention used for pr-12..pr-17 F4 artifacts.
